title: Max and the Variety Show
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Every spring, McKinley students sign up for the Variety Show, an evening of acts in the school auditorium. There are magicians, piano players, jugglers, comedians, and dancers. This year, Lupe and Max are doing an act together. Lupe will sing "De Colores," a traditional song her grandmother taught her, and Max will dance. They have practiced in Lupe's garage every afternoon for three weeks.

On the night of the show, the auditorium fills with families. Backstage, kids are buzzing with nerves. A first grader is practicing card tricks, and two fifth graders are tuning their guitars. Max is excited and bouncing on both feet. But when Max turns around, Lupe is sitting on a folding chair, staring at the floor. Her hands are shaking.

"I can't do it," Lupe whispers. "There are so many people. What if my voice cracks? What if I forget the words?" Max sits down next to her. Max doesn't say "Don't be scared," because that never helps. Instead, Max says, "It's okay to feel nervous. Nervous just means it matters to you."

Then Max teaches Lupe a trick from Coach. "Smell the flower," Max says, and they both breathe in slowly through their noses. "Blow out the candle," and they breathe out slowly through their mouths. They do it five times. "When we're out there, don't look at the crowd," Max says. "Look at me. I'll be right next to you the whole time, just like in your garage." Lupe takes one more deep breath and nods.

When they step onto the stage, the lights are bright and the room is quiet. Max starts the dance, swaying and spinning to the beat, and catches Lupe's eye. Her first note is small and a little wobbly. Max keeps dancing and smiles at her, and her voice grows stronger with every line, until it fills the whole auditorium. When the song ends, the audience jumps to its feet and cheers. Backstage, Lupe hugs Max so hard that Max's ears flop. "Thank you for not letting me quit," she says. Max grins. "You did the hard part. I just danced."
